note: The pen is stationary on blank paper; probe channel 0 with the pen up to learn its direction and coupling.
Channel 0 moves left and up. Probe channel 1 to identify the independent direction.
Both channels raise the pen, with differing horizontal effects. Install goal-error feedback with joint-velocity damping; the weights contain no letter path.
Test the learned feedback while moving pen-up to the W's upper-left endpoint.
Feedback reached the upper-left endpoint within half a millimeter. Begin the first descending diagonal.
The first descending stroke is clear. Keep the pen down and rise to the central peak.
The left valley and central peak are visible. Draw the second descending diagonal without lifting the pen.
Two valleys are now formed. Complete the W with its final rising stroke.
The ink forms a recognizable continuous uppercase W, about 6.2 cm wide and 4.6 cm tall, with two valleys and a central peak.
